touches.text: artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

The one writer question is LLM or code, and only for gate-pass certificates; who authored a write is not tracked otherwise. So on Windows the caller class comes from the process chain: claude.exe above the writer means cc; otherwise it is not cc. Env vars are a fallback only. Certificates are made where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), so Windows does not need a gate class of its own. - CC

CC over ssh is told from Akien by the key sshd accepted: CC on each box gets a dedicated ssh key. Until it lands, approve and the operator close refuse any sshd-session caller, Akien's included (Q#115). -amm

It grows into a claude_code user per box: Cairn runs as akien, and superclaude launches the claude executable as claude_code. Over ssh, CC logs in as claude_code where it can and launches claude there. WHY: the user id is the kernel's word for who wrote what, not an asserted variable. -amm

claude_code is an admin, elevating on request rather than standing elevated, and CC may talk to other CCs over the inter-CC messaging and use ssh to set up and fix boxes like an IT admin. WHY: Akien uses CC for IT work on his boxes, and two CCs together can fix what one box alone cannot see. -amm

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).

Any device may ask Recovery to run something as root. The operator answers each ask: decline, accept now, accept always, accept with a new rule, or (for a chat-enabled device) chat about it. Cairn owns it.
